evaluationCost.note: evaluation cost; never added to arm cost

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The change adds no new domain rule. Hold queue order comes from the Tier 2 call Holds.queueFor. Branch validation and the shelf contents come from the existing shelf view, which the change reuses. The new Tier 3 code only orders rows by id, formats them as CSV and builds the status text from the existing DueBack value. That is projection, not rule-making.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: All three new exports write through the existing Files port, and the Ports record is unchanged. The new code does not read the clock and does no direct I/O. The existing exportOverdue still calls File.WriteAllLines directly. That violation was already there and the change leaves it alone. The unknown-branch case returns an error before any write.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The member CSV layout `member,type,name` is now written here and parsed separately by importMembers. The two sites agree, and a round-trip test checks that they do, but nothing ties them to one definition, so they can drift. Everything else has a single definition. Hold order comes from Holds.queueFor, and member type names come from the existing memberTypeName.

evidence.quote: Catalog.addCopy { Id = CopyId copyId; Book = BookId bookId; Branch = branch } library

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Validation of a new copy (duplicate or unknown copy or book) stays in Tier 2 through Catalog.addCopy, and branch lookup uses Catalog.findBranch. The hold count comes from Tier 2's Holds.queueFor. Tier 3 only parses CSV lines, numbers the error line and formats the status label. All of that is translation and projection.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The CSV is read through the existing Files port and saved through the existing commit helper. The CLI only dispatches to the use case. The new code adds no clock, no direct I/O and no console use below Tier 4. Tier 4 does not re-enter Tier 2. The hold-count view logic is pure.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The number of holds on a book is derived once, from the Tier 2 queue, and not recounted. Copy validity is defined only in Catalog.addCopy. The line-numbering and error-wrapping pattern follows importMembers, but it is only plumbing and is not a domain fact.
